findings.flow: F09 filing lifecycle / RULE-012 package completeness
findings.title: A proof-required filing can reach SUBMISSION with an empty declared package (purpose-blind criteria guard)
findings.trigger: Create a filing with proofRequired=true and declare exactly one mandatory criterion with purpose=OUTCOME; advance PACKAGE_PREPARATION → SIGNATURE → SUBMISSION.
findings.steps: See r2/walkthrough-evidence/gw03-narrative.md 'Filing F (outcome-only criterion probe)' and calls.jsonl (filing 01a192b8-4110-7bb4…).
findings.expected: RULE-012/state-semantics: package completeness requires declared applicable documents/signature criteria before submission; zero applicable package criteria must not silently open the gate.
findings.actual: PACKAGE_PREPARATION passed (guard counts ANY non-retired criterion on the filing, regardless of purpose — filing.go:355-364), and SUBMISSION succeeded with `package.declared=false, total=0` (vacuous satisfaction over mandatory PACKAGE criteria). The filing record then reads stage=SUBMISSION, execution=WAITING, outcomeVerification=PENDING.
findings.evidence: apps/backend/internal/core/domain/matter/filing.go:355-364 (n counts criteria without purpose filter); live HTTP: submission accepted, proof readback {package:{declared:false,total:0,mandatory:0}}.
findings.suggested_correction: Require at least one non-retired PACKAGE-purpose criterion for PACKAGE_PREPARATION when proof is required (or explicit OWNER declaration), and refuse SUBMISSION while package.declared=false; keep the BF-01 outcome semantics untouched. Business-level change: state-semantics filing table gains an explicit 'zero declared package criteria refuses submission' row.
findings.acceptance_to_add: Filing with only an OUTCOME criterion is refused at PACKAGE_PREPARATION with package-criteria-required; submission refused while package.declared=false; recorded AC-163 variant.

findings.flow: F09 filing lifecycle / RULE-011 signature completeness
findings.title: For proof-required filings the signature gate accepts any satisfied mandatory criterion; no signature-specific criterion kind exists
findings.trigger: Filing A in GW-03: proofRequired=true, one generic PACKAGE criterion ('package complete on submitted version') accepted; no signature observation was ever recorded; SIGNATURE→SUBMISSION succeeded.
findings.steps: r2/walkthrough-evidence/gw03-narrative.md filing A; contrast filing C (proofRequired=false) which was refused `signature-required` until a signature observation existed.
findings.expected: RULE-011: signature completeness is a separate observation/criterion, never inferred from current-version status or upload success; GW-01/GW-03 expect signature tracking to be visible.
findings.actual: filing.go:379-394 proves signatures for proof-required filings through 'its mandatory criteria' — any satisfied mandatory criterion covers signatures, so a generic package criterion (no signature semantics) opens the submission gate with zero signature observations. No-proof filings ARE guarded (observation or OWNER no-signature decision required). The asymmetry is purpose-blind in the same way as Z-F-01.
findings.evidence: apps/backend/internal/core/domain/matter/filing.go:379-394; live: filing A submission 200 with signatures=[] on the submitted version.
findings.suggested_correction: Either require, for proof-required filings, at least one satisfied criterion that references signature observations (extend criterion with a signature-binding flag), or require the OWNER's signature-applicability decision for every filing before SUBMISSION (today it is only consulted for no-proof filings). Business-level: define in state-semantics how a signature criterion is recognized.
findings.acceptance_to_add: Submission refused when the only satisfied criteria carry no signature semantics and no OWNER signature decision exists; positive path with a real signature criterion; OWNER no-signature applicability honored.

findings.flow: F09 filing lifecycle / BF-01 residual (corroborates remediation §9 and r1)
findings.title: Filing without a declared OUTCOME criterion discloses NOT_DECLARED, but grids/Control Room keep the package-driven aggregate
findings.trigger: Open a filing list/Control Room/Grid for a filing whose package criteria are satisfied but which declares no OUTCOME criterion.
findings.expected: BF-01 acceptance: the pending/absent outcome is visible wherever the filing's verification is shown.
findings.actual: Filing detail, filing list rows and the filing's work-item detail carry `outcomeVerification:NOT_DECLARED` (verified live); grids and Control Room still render the package-driven `verification` only (they do not know filing-ness). Whether APPROVAL should require a declared OUTCOME criterion remains open PO decision D-BF1.
findings.evidence: Live: `{ver:…, ov:NOT_DECLARED}` on filing detail; matter-control Control Room sections unchanged.
findings.suggested_correction: Product decision needed (PO): either accept the two-surface disclosure, or thread filing-ness (outcomeVerification) into the grid/Control Room rows.
findings.acceptance_to_add: A manager reading the Grid or Control Room cannot mistake package readiness for outcome acceptance, without expanding the read model beyond the approved baseline.

findings.title: Receipted commands validate the Idempotency-Key (400) before authorization (403/404)
findings.trigger: VIEWER posts /matters/{id}/evidence without an Idempotency-Key; VIEWER posts /bulk/commit with an empty rows array.
findings.steps: r2/walkthrough-evidence/gw01-narrative.md 'TRAP viewer-submit-evidence'; traps2 'viewer bulk commit denied'.
findings.expected: Contract §3 error precedence puts forbidden (403) before key checks; the permission matrix expects a uniform denial for unauthorized writes.
findings.actual: Both cases return `400 urn:mc:bad-request` (key required / malformed) rather than the uniform 403. No data leaks (the body names only the missing key), but an unauthorized caller learns validation order.
findings.suggested_correction: Run authorization before key validation on receipted commands, or accept and document the current order in local-contract §3.
findings.acceptance_to_add: AC-134 variant asserting uniform denial for unauthorized receipted commands regardless of key presence.

findings.flow: F03 matter membership / contract §2.2 CAS mapping
findings.title: Matter-members grant with a stale If-Match answers 403 instead of the documented 412
findings.trigger: Owner grants a matter member using an ETag captured before another membership change bumped the matter revision.
findings.steps: r2/walkthrough-evidence/gw02-narrative.md 'dung has explicit VIEWER' (grant 403 with a stale-but-readable matter ETag).
findings.expected: local-contract §2.2: 'an equal tag maps to the current revision, any other tag to a stale revision (412)'.
findings.actual: 403 forbidden was returned (observed once, live). Denial is safe (no mutation) but the documented stale path did not fire.
findings.evidence: calls.jsonl POST /matters/{id}/members status 403 with a stale If-Match; contrast gw01 member grants (fresh ETag) 200.
findings.suggested_correction: Verify the ETag→revision mapping used by the members command (canonical representation may include caller-dependent members); make stale map to 412 or amend §2.2.
findings.acceptance_to_add: AC-139 variant on membership commands: stale tag → 412 with current revision, no mutation.

findings.title: WAITING requires an internal owner set via a separate metadata PATCH first
findings.trigger: POST execution {to:WAITING, reason, waitingPartyId, waitingCondition} on an action with ownerId=null.
findings.steps: r2/walkthrough-evidence/gw02-narrative.md 'AC-104' (first attempt 409 waiting-owner-required, then PATCH owner, then WAITING).
findings.expected: FR-004 requires reason + accountable internal owner — the guard is correct — but the journey needs two commands where the form suggests one.
findings.actual: 409 waiting-owner-required until ownerId is PATCHed; after that the transition succeeds.
findings.evidence: calls.jsonl (waiting-owner-required then success); matches r1 finding F-06.
findings.suggested_correction: Accept owner in the execution command for the WAITING target, or surface the required owner field in the same form.
findings.acceptance_to_add: One-command WAITING with owner+party; guard messages name the missing fields.

findings.title: Live OUTCOME_UNKNOWN drill not executed (needs fault injection); unknown-key paths verified uniform-404
findings.trigger: Simulated transport loss after a possible commit.
findings.steps: Not performed in r2; r1 reached the same boundary.
findings.expected: RULE-018/AC-153: unknown outcome is exposed as OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and reconciled via the stored receipt.
findings.actual: NOT_VERIFIED here: no fault injection was attempted. Verified instead: same-key replay (`Idempotent-Replayed:true`, no duplicate) and unknown-key `GET /operations/{key}` + reconciliation → uniform 404. The OUTCOME_UNKNOWN path itself is covered by the green W6 contract suites (author-run).
findings.evidence: r2/walkthrough-evidence/traps2-narrative.md F15 lines; backend suite exit 0 (r2 window).
findings.suggested_correction: A dedicated recovery drill (kill between commit and response) belongs to the independent QA track.
findings.acceptance_to_add: AC-153 executed with a real interrupted write.
